---
title: "Organizations"
subtitle: "Documented names and roles — not organizational histories"
---

This page tracks organizations named in the evidence. A listing means only that the archive can connect a name to a public source or an identified research lead; it does **not** establish legal continuity, institutional responsibility, or a role in creating CSIL.

Where inspected sources describe a function, that function is stated narrowly. Where a name comes only from early project notes, it remains labelled that way.

## Names first identified in project notes

| Name as first listed for this archive | Why the name appears here |
| --- | --- |
| BC Rehabilitation Society (also “BC Rehab”) | Named as creator of *Keys on Freedom* and, with Greater Vancouver Home Support Society, of ECPM manual(s) |
| Greater Vancouver Home Support Society | Named with BC Rehab on ECPM manual(s) |
| Ryan & Wiggins | Named with Patricia Ryan on the Creekview 202 evaluation; not independently confirmed on an inspected title page |
| British Columbia Ministry of Health, Continuing Care Division / Community Support Branch | Named as the likely administrative home of 1993–95 CSIL pilot/design records; the HEU *Guardian* Nov/Dec 1995 independently places a new/pilot CSIL program there |
| British Columbia Ministry of Health Services | Named on the cover and prepared-by page of the November 2008 synthesis report |
| James Murtagh Consulting | Named as preparer on the November 2008 synthesis report's prepared-by page |

Some of these names also appear in inspected public sources. For example, BC Rehab and Greater Vancouver Home Support Society appear in the [Roeher bibliography](../sources/1990s-roeher-if-bibliography.qmd), while the Ministry of Health Services and James Murtagh Consulting appear on the [2008 Program Review Synthesis Report](../sources/2008-program-review-synthesis.qmd).

## Organizations in inspected Creekview-period sources

The table below records only functions described in sources that have been inspected. See the [Creekview chapter](../history/creekview.qmd) for the narrative context.

| Name as it appears in inspected sources | Documented function in those sources | Sources |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Creekview Co-op / Creekview Cooperative / Creekview 202 | Housing cooperative apartment / “integrated self managed independent living project” near False Creek; not treated here as a corporate CSIL entity | [Hansard 1984](../sources/1984-hansard-mowat-creekview.qmd); [Hansard 1986](../sources/1986-hansard-nielsen-creekview.qmd); [Haw 1989](../sources/1989-haw-special-housing-needs.qmd) |
| Pearson Hospital (later also “George Pearson Hospital”) | Extended-care setting residents left; Haw and the 1987 abstract say Pearson continued to support Creekview | Same Hansard sittings; Haw 1989; [Mattinson and Rompf 1987 abstract](../sources/1987-mattinson-rompf-creekview.qmd); [Fayerman 2018](../sources/2018-vancouversun-walt-lawrence.qmd) |
| Canadian Paraplegic Association / BCPA (later SCI BC) | Haw: co-developer of Creekview 202 and funding conduit; Nielsen: sent the minister a photograph. Later SCI BC history claims the 1985 opening | Haw 1989; Hansard 1986; [SCI BC history](../sources/sci-bc-history.qmd) |
| British Columbia Ministry of Health | Nielsen: one of the “government agencies” that allowed the independent group setting; Haw: funding through CPA; 1987 abstract: evaluation party | Hansard 1986; Haw 1989; Mattinson and Rompf 1987 abstract |
| Workers Compensation Board | Haw: funding to tenants through CPA, with the ministry | Haw 1989 |
| Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC) | Haw: funded the 100-unit cooperative building | Haw 1989 |

Creekview remains a [history chapter](../history/creekview.qmd), rather than an organization record, because the inspected sources describe a co-op apartment or project and do not establish a separate corporate form.

Future organization records should keep documented functions separate from later attributions and link each claim to a [source record](../sources/index.qmd).
